ms.report:
Kia ora Cardano, Project Catalyst whanau.
Thank you for your support of our TribalDID’s=Indigenous Sovereignty Project, which is now finally moving towards its final stages. 
This phase, although small in scope, has been one of the most challenging. 
Working on the innovative edge of digital identity for the hapori (communities) we serve — starting with those closest, in Aotearoa and alongside the Atala PRISM tribe, who are focused primarily on commercial applications of digital identity, has highlighted how the hypotheses at the start of a project shapes the work and what is prioritised.
We submitted an update on this Phase in September 2023. You can find that here. At that point our project was 3 months beyond the timeline we had envisaged. The combination of our requirements to maintain trusted relationships with our whanau (including a commitment to only work with Open Source technology, to build for offline, p2p and p4p use cases) and the Atala PRISM timeline to contribute code to an Open Source project host for the Cardano based identity solution had slowed progress substantially. In fact, it wasn't until December 2023 that Atala PRISM, a suite of decentralized identity tools, became "Open Enterprise Agent", an Open Source code base in Hyperledger Labs. Although causing our project to fall behind its timeline, the move was a win-win, guaranteeing the Open Source future of the codebase hosted by an organisation dedicated to global frameworks, open standards, tools and libraries to build blockchains, related applications and meeting the Digital and Data Sovereignty requirements of our people.
Since then, further delays have occurred related to the stability of the code and the necessity to build additional infrastructure ourselves that has not become part of the Atala roadmap (and contribute it back to the Open Source project) and other activities taking place and prioritised by the Project Catalyst team.

Kia ora Cardano, Project Catalyst whanau.
Thank you for your support of our TribalDID’s=Indigenous Sovereignty Project.
It’s been an incredible experience for us and the whanau we serve to be supported to work on this future-facing project which has the potential for so much more for impact than has already been achieved.
You can find the explanation, video, evidence of achievements and deliverables for our Phase 5 OKRs detailed and linked in the following Deck and Report. To close-out this project and find details of what’s next, see our final close-out video and report.
Your support of this TribalDID’s=Indigenous Sovereignty Project is deeply appreciated. It has enabled us to explore and begin the journey towards a new future for our Māori hapori (community) and indigenous peoples globally.
